title: The Runaway Slave
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Slave, being discontented with his lot, ran away from his master. He was soon missed by the latter, who lost no time in mounting his horse and setting out in pursuit of the fugitive. He presently came up with him, and the Slave, in the hope of avoiding capture, slipped into a treadmill and hid himself there. "Aha," said his master, "that's the very place for you, my man!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Slave run away from his master?
options: He wanted to find a new master
He was discontented with his lot
He was ordered to leave by his master
He wanted to explore new places

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the master do as soon as he missed the Slave?
options: Waited for him to return on his own
Mounted his horse and set out in pursuit

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what word does it use for the escaped Slave during the chase?
According to the passage, where did the Slave hide to avoid capture?
According to the passage, what did the master say once he found the Slave?
options: "Run all you like, I will always find you"
"That's the very place for you, my man!"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fugitive" mean in "in pursuit of the fugitive"?
As the passage uses it, what does "discontented" mean in "being discontented with his lot"?
Based on the passage, why is the master's remark likely meant as an ironic jab at the Slave?
options: Because a treadmill was a device of hard forced labor, so the Slave has hidden himself in a symbol of the toil he tried to escape
Because the master genuinely believes treadmills are comfortable hiding spots
Because the Slave requested to be placed in the treadmill
Because treadmills were reserved for free citizens, not slaves

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how quickly was the Slave missed by his master?
According to the passage, what did the Slave hope to avoid by hiding in the treadmill?
In the phrase "He was soon missed by the latter," who does "the latter" refer to?
As the passage uses it, what does "lot" mean in "discontented with his lot"?
options: A parcel of land he owned
His condition or situation in life

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the master's ironic remark suggest about how a treadmill was normally used?
options: As a comfortable resting place for animals
As a device of hard, forced labor
As a place where slaves were rewarded
As a device used only for grinding spices

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Slave successfully escapes and is never found
A master frees his Slave after finding him in a treadmill
A Slave runs away out of discontent, but when his master catches him hiding in a treadmill, the master mocks that he has ended up in a fitting place of toil
A Slave is punished by being placed in a treadmill for a full year
